text:
Sam C: Quick alert — after the kernel-selection change (roll 2140000000) last night we see KV cache hit-rate down ~8% on canary and gpu1 memory spikes leading to 2x OOM retries. attaching short logs.
Ajay: link to roll/commit?
Sam C: commit d4f7b9a, rollout to canary only. https://git.internal/r/roll/2140000000
Maya: looked at flamegraphs. fused attention path is allocating a larger scratch buffer for some sequence-length combos. small prefix keys now end up on GPU with larger per-key footprint.
Maya: snippet from perf-run (canary):
```
kv_prefill_hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.64
gpu1_mem_used: 82% -> 96% under steady load
oom_events: 1 -> 3 in last 30m
kernel_path: fused_fast -> fallback_slow for ~15% requests
```
Jen H: interesting — fused_fast was supposed to reduce latency but it's increasing transient memory due to bigger workspace. could cause LRU churn and fragmentation.
Ajay: do we have a quick mitigant? revert roll or runtime toggle?
Sam C: we can flip runtime flag to prefer small-workspace kernels under memory pressure. I want to avoid full revert until we fully understand perf tradeoffs.
Maya: proposal: staged TTL probe + compact-on-idle + kernel-fallback rule.
Maya: details:
- short probe TTL for new prefixes (10s) to avoid immediately filling GPU cache with heavy keys
- when GPU free < 15% trigger compact sweep to coalesce fragments
- kernel fallback: if estimated workspace > X bytes and free_gpu < threshold, pick narrow-workspace kernel even if slightly slower
Ajay: +1. should also adjust LRU weight to prefer keys with high access frequency (not just recency) for a short window after rollout.
Jen H: I'll push a canary config: `runtime.kernel_preference=mem_safe` and `kv.probe_ttl=10s` to the canary pool and run a 1h replay with yesterday's traffic.
perf-bot: auto-metric: canary/2140001234 kv_prefill_hit_rate: -7.9% vs baseline, oom_rate +3.8% (30m)
Sam C: thanks. Jen, after replay please grab new kv key distributions and per-prefix hit histogram.
Jen H: on it. planning deploy in 5m. I'll post results in this thread.
Maya: one more thought — compaction should be spread (rate limit) and use idle GPU cycles only. full compaction causes stalls.
Ajay: agree. add compaction backoff if kernel-switch latency > 50ms.
Jen H: deployed mem_safe canary. replay started. will post early signals in ~15m.
perf-bot: replay/2140001234 early: kv_prefill_hit_rate -3.6%, gpu_mem_peak 88%, oom_events 0 (first 15m)
Sam C: early signal looks better than rollback case. keeping kernel_preference for now while we gather full-hour metrics. thanks team.
Maya: follow-ups:
- run per-model seq-len bucketing to see which buckets drive workspace blowup
- quantify latency delta between fused vs mem_safe paths (p95)
- simulate TTL smoothing (gradual increase from 10s -> 60s) to see hit-rate tradeoffs
Ajay: I'll own the LRU weighting experiment.
Jen H: will post full 1h results in ~40m. if stable we can promote config to prod canary across all pools.
Sam C: plan and owners noted. tagging infra for a potential short rollback window if OOMs spike: @infra-team :alert:
perf-bot: full replay/2140001234 (1h): kv_prefill_hit_rate -1.1% vs baseline, gpu_mem_peak 85%, oom_events 0, p95 added latency on mem_safe path +6ms.
Sam C: looks acceptable tradeoff. moving forward: 1) promote mem_safe kernel pref to more canaries 2) start compaction-on-idle rollout 3) run TTL-smoothing A/B test. I'll create tracking tickets.
Jen H: created tickets INF-2141 (kernel-pref rollout), ENGRT-2142 (compaction staged), PERF-2143 (TTL A/B). linking here.
Sam C: thanks — we'll close this thread after postmortem if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
